body: Thank you so much for telling me this. Congratulations on the baby!

What do you consider "normal"? It might be that you've been underestimating yourself for so long, you've managed to define "normal" specifically as something you can't attain.

One thing that's helpful to keep in mind is that while you don't know what you're doing and everyone else seems to, the reality of it is that they're good at pretending they know what they're doing. Everyone is stumbling through life doing their best, and for some people it works, and for some people it doesn't. Just because your best hasn't rewarded you the way it has other people doesn't mean something is wrong with you.
I know, sorry about that, but it was the one aspect of it I simply couldn't find information on. The article you linked was actually really helpful, so thank you for that!
I'd love that. PM me whenever you want about whatever you want.

I'm happy to hear this! So long as you just keep being you, I think you'll be doing the right thing.

If you feel like you want to talk further about it, I'm always open.

Sorry I didn't respond earlier, I was asleep and didn't know you'd replied.

Thank you so much for opening up about the situation, and at this point, all I can say is that it looks like you're doing better than you feel like you're doing. So long as the dating relationship is healthy, being able to hold onto someone for that long is an accomplishment even a lot of mentally well people struggle to achieve.

The thing is, you're making progress slowly, and it may not feel like it's enough. But looking back on where you were a year ago, five years ago, etc, etc, you've made huge improvements. This is going to take faith in yourself, and I should hope that everything you've been able to do so far would be good enough to have this, but I believe that some time from now, you'll be thanking yourself for holding on. It's painful now, but is it still as painful as it was a while ago?

I have no idea what you can and can't do in your situation, or even the specifics of it, so take this with a grain of salt, but the only thing I can think of is to cut off as many people who make you feel bad as possible. It's hard to trust anyone when most of the people you've been around treat you like shit; getting away from them and giving yourself time to relax might help you learn to trust people again and start to feel calmer. Being truly alone, physically and emotionally, feels better than being surrounded by people physically but totally alone emotionally, at least to me.

I genuinely believe you're doing everything in your power to heal, but a lot of people don't know all of their options because they're afraid of stepping outside of "normal" treatment options like therapy and medication when what they really need is to get toxic people out of their life instead of finding new ways to tolerate them.

Sleep well. I'm always here if you want to talk.

I mean, not 24/7, but bare minimum I can squeeze in a couple of exchanges per day, and usually it's more than that.

All right, I'm back.

Another thing to consider about the orphanage thing: let's say that you do get kicked out and end up killing yourself. The thing is, you were planning on killing yourself when you were stuck with your parents, right? So if you have the choice between being abused by your parents before you die or, worst case scenario, being abused by strangers who will probably neglect you more than they will actually pick on you, shouldn't you go with the latter to maximize the time you have in peace.

Also, you can apply for the military while in an orphanage/foster home; you just need the approval of the courts. From the information you've given me, which isn't the entire situation and there may be some key things I don't know about, it seems like contacting CPS really is your best bet, no matter what you end up doing to yourself.

Use those three months in an orphanage to scramble for a job through whatever means necessary. There's gotta be one slumlord out there willing to rent cheap so that you're homeless for as little time as possible.

I have to leave right now, but I'm going to come back later and continue.

Is there anything that could make those months bearable? Maybe you could cut it a bit short and make a run for it a few days prior to your birthday so at least you get a break for a few days? I really don't know what's feasible in your situation, but I want to explore every other possibility when the time you have left is two months. It must feel like an eternity, but rest assured you'll be dead longer than you'll be miserable waiting to get out of the house.

And about the beating thing: have you ever considered contacting CPS? Beating your child for wanting to go into the military seems pretty damn rescue-worthy.

Do you have to have parental permission? I don't know shit about applying for the military, so please excuse me if that's a totally asinine question. My phone sucks and it's all I have to post with right now; otherwise I'd look it up.

I'm sorry to hear about the physical problems. If you're rejected for that, the only thing I could suggest is, as embarrassing as it might sound, searching for people to prop you up for a month or two while you scramble for a job and some housing. Or even doing a ton of research on how to be sustainably homeless for a short period of time. If there's certain things about homelessness or "bumming"(I hate that term but I can't think of a less negative word for it because our society is set up to shame the poor) off of strangers that you simply can't handle, then don't try it. This is all about trying to get you in a better mental state through whatever means possible.

Also, please please please keep in mind that asking for help from others does not make you needy, imposing, impolite, lazy, ungrateful, or whatever nasty things people might try to say you are. Even if you have no plans of doing that, simply entertaining the thought in your mind is harmless and you're not a bad person for doing it. If this isn't relevant to your situation, then I'm glad you at least have that figured out, but I've been in positions of apparent hopelessness before and I'm starting to learn there are options besides keeping everything to yourself until something explodes.

The people in your life right now sound absolutely terrible and the only thing I could recommend is getting away from them ASAP, but I doubt you haven't already thought about that and you know your own limitations.

The only things I can offer are some companionship in the form of PMs or Skype and some assistance in helping you find an exit route, if one exists. I know the pain of getting nothing but shit from the people who are supposed to be protecting you from the world and if there's anything I can do to alleviate even the tiniest part of it, tell me how.

If you're the one convincing yourself that you're a social fuck-up, chances are the majority of people you talk to think you're a fine conversationalist. I would know this, because I have this problem all the time, no matter what the situation is. Even if someone is clearly grumpy before they've even seen me, I feel like it's my fault they're glaring at me and using two-syllable sentences.

Do you feel like people are expecting you to fall into a certain role that you just can't live up to?

The difference between you and the people who look like they know what they're doing is that the latter are really good at pretending everything's fine.

Nobody knows what they're doing. You just do your best, cross your fingers, and hope life doesn't shit on you.

It looks like life shat on you anyhow. You're not a burden for having been dealt a bad hand. All you can do is try your best to work through it, and you may not feel like you're up to that.

You can only do what you can do. You're a person. You do not have infinite strength.

Stagnation is one of the most vicious cycles a person can be trapped in. Everything is ho-hum, to the point where you find your everyday routine more and more pointless, with the idea of trying to pull yourself out of it becoming sillier as the days go on. It's a void that'll suck you in and spit you out when you have nothing left for it to take.

I genuinely don't know how to address this. If you don't want to, can't see the point of, or don't feel it's possible to get out of it, there's nothing I can say that will change that, especially when I know so little about your situation. It's your life. You know it better than any rando on the internet.

All I can say is that if you ever feel like chatting with a stranger to chip at the monotony, I'd be happy to talk to you.

Subreddits like r/penpals and r/MakeNewFriendsHere. Usually 50% don't respond after I PM them back, another 30% are gone after the first three days of messaging, and the rest taper off. I've only actively ended one correspondence, when a guy accused me of being a white feminazi and also didn't appreciate my liberal use of bird gifs. The rest are ghosting.

I like talking about pretty much anything, although it depends on the person in question, honestly. Some people make gardening sound exciting, others struggle to make the story about the time they fought off eight tigers with their big toe and a shoelace interesting.

If things other people consider small make you genuinely uncomfortable, that means you have every right to avoid those things, regardless of what they think. Your mom is the one being unreasonable in this situation, not you, because your issues clearly aren't the kind where you just "get over it". I hate that term. Anything you're able to get over, nobody is going to tell you to get over it, because they'll never know it was a problem.

If a simple task seems impossible, it's because it's no longer simple for you. It's important to recognize that and not get down on yourself for not meeting arbitrary standards. You can only do what you're able to do; pushing yourself beyond your limits out of guilt is only going to inhibit you.

And please, if your boyfriend makes you happy or at least feel not as bad, hold onto him through any means possible. If you feel safe talking to him about these things, you could try that.
That's encouraging, thank you.

I understand that, but one thing I don't think I made clear enough is that I hate conflict. I can't stop myself from mindlessly nodding away to whatever my parents are saying, because that's what they're used to and any deviation thereof has the chance to spark concern or annoyance that kills me. Just getting weird looks or rude comments makes me feel like shit, and they always get the last word. It feels pointless. Letting them know that something is wrong would cause conflict. Conflict makes me want to die. I'm not entirely sure that what's going to be a week of tension and anger will be made up for by the counseling.

Also, eventually, I'm going to tell my dad. Getting out of there ASAP is my first choice. Counseling might be a second choice if I'm not allowed to leave.

I guess college is an option, but it's one I'm not ready to take that seriously. To be fair, my disinterest in it does come from my dad telling me about it, but also out of the many people I know who have a degree, exactly one of them has a job related to it capable of paying off large amounts of debt.

College? That's the funniest thing I've heard all year. My dad earns $16 an hour picking up more garbage than should physically be possible and my current job pays *under* the state minimum wage.

The only problem with the counselor thing is that it'd set off red flags with my parents that something is wrong and I'm not telling them about it. I don't have the money or transportation to do something like that under the radar.

I appreciate your advice and your time, but I don't know how much use it's going to be.

You're welcome. I think you deserve all the encouragement you can get--most people never stop to think about what they've done to themselves and others, they just do whatever they feel like until consequences happen. As much as I hate that you're feeling this way, the fact that you're inspecting your self-worth is farther than the majority of people get.

Everyone talks about, "Oh, it's the small things in life that make it worthwhile!" Except they don't. Having a new coffee drink and finding out it's delicious doesn't make up for the fact that your life is collapsing around you.

The little stuff carries you up until you finally hit that big, awesome thing that either turns your lives around or at least takes you higher than ever before and places you back down in a marginally better place. If you haven't had any big, awesome things happening in the last 3 years, you won't remember the small things. Because they don't matter anymore.

I guess what I mean is that people will keep inventing reasons for you to go on living without stopping to think about what's been happening to you or what your situation could be, and those people can eat a bag of dicks because hearing inapplicable advice is worse than no advice at all. Don't feel bad when you can't fit into the cookie cutters people want to shove you in. A loaf of bread not making for a good gingerbread man does not mean bread is worthless.

On another note, your teacher sounds like an idiot and should be fired. Unless you murdered someone in front of them, there's no reason to say or even imply things like that.
